DB-E4.Description:
Create consent record schema and database table for time-bounded authorization.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/schemas/consent.py: ConsentRecord, ConsentRequest, ConsentAuditLog models
- Fields: id, user_id, service, scope, consent_type (session/time_bounded/recurring), granted_at, expires_at, times_used, revoked_at
- Create database migration for consent_records table
- Add unique constraint on (user_id, service)
- Create consent_audit_log table for compliance
- Add indexes on user_id and expires_at for query performance

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-011

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Models validate correctly
- Database migration runs cleanly
- Unique constraint enforced
- Audit log captures all events

EDGE CASES:
- Duplicate consent: update existing record
- Expired consent: query filters by expires_at
- Revoked consent: soft delete with revoked_at

Create consent management endpoints for granting, viewing, and revoking consent.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/api/v1/consent.py router
- POST /api/v1/consent: grant consent with service, scope, ttl_hours
- GET /api/v1/consent: list active consents for user
- DELETE /api/v1/consent/{id}: revoke consent
- Calculate expires_at from ttl_hours (default 4 hours for calendar)
- Log all consent operations to audit table
- Return ConsentRecord in response

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-029

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Grant creates consent record
- List returns only active (non-expired, non-revoked)
- Revoke sets revoked_at
- Audit log captures all operations

EDGE CASES:
- Grant for existing service: update expires_at
- Revoke non-existent: return 404
- List with no consents: return empty array

Create frontend modal for JIT (Just-In-Time) consent prompts.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create frontend/components/ConsentPromptModal.tsx
- Props: request (ConsentRequest), onGrant, onDeny, isLoading
- Display: service name, requested scopes, suggested TTL
- Allow user to select TTL: 'This briefing only', '1 hour', '4 hours', '24 hours'
- Call POST /api/v1/consent on grant
- Trigger OAuth redirect for Google Calendar
- Show loading state during OAuth flow
- Accessible: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Frontend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-030

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Modal renders with correct content
- TTL selection works
- Grant triggers API call
- Deny closes modal without action

EDGE CASES:
- OAuth popup blocked: show instruction
- OAuth error: show error message
- Multiple scopes: list all clearly

Update Orchestrator to handle consent_required escalations from Calendar Agent.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Update backend/agents/orchestrator/node.py
- Check for consent_required escalation in calendar_result
- Pause graph execution when consent required
- Return partial response with awaiting_consent status
- Include consent_request in response for frontend
- Resume graph after consent granted (via new request)
- Store partial state for resume (optional checkpointing)

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-017, DB-029

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Consent required pauses graph
- Response includes consent_request
- New request after consent succeeds
- Partial state preserved correctly

EDGE CASES:
- Consent denied: return degraded briefing without calendar
- Consent expires mid-graph: re-request
- Multiple services need consent: batch requests

Configure Local LLM fallback in LLMRouter for privacy-sensitive data.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Update backend/settings.py with LOCAL_LLM_ENABLED, LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL, LOCAL_LLM_MODEL_ID
- Update backend/llm/router.py with fallback logic
- Fallback triggers: rate limit (429), timeout, PII data classification
- Local LLM uses OpenAI-compatible API (llama.cpp server)
- Track fallback events in metrics (llm_fallback_total counter)
- Document supported models in docs/LOCAL-LLM.md

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-016

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Fallback triggered on rate limit
- Fallback triggered on timeout
- PII forces local LLM
- Fallback metrics recorded

EDGE CASES:
- Local LLM disabled: no fallback, raise error
- Local LLM unavailable: raise error with context
- Both fail: aggregate error message

Implement learner feedback loop for user preference extraction.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/schemas/preferences.py: UserPreference model
- Create user_preferences table via migration
- Create POST /api/v1/preferences/feedback endpoint
- Accept: briefing_id, edited_content
- Orchestrator analyzes delta between original and edited
- Extract preference (e.g., 'prefers morning deep work')
- Store preference with confidence score
- Inject preferences into Focus Agent context on subsequent runs

EFFORT: L (6 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-017

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Feedback endpoint accepts edits
- Preference extracted from delta
- Preferences loaded for next briefing
- Confidence scores reasonable

EDGE CASES:
- No edits: don't extract preference
- Conflicting preferences: keep highest confidence
- User deletes preference: remove from context

Create data export endpoint for GDPR compliance.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:
- Create backend/api/v1/export.py router
- GET /api/v1/export: export all user data as JSON
- Include: user profile, preferences, tasks, briefing history, consent records, DLQ events
- Rate limit: 5 requests per hour
- Support format parameter: json (default), csv
- Async generation for large exports
- Return download URL for async exports

EFFORT: M (4 hours)
PROJECT AREA: Backend
DEPENDENCIES: DB-034, DB-029

TESTING CRITERIA:
- Export includes all data categories
- JSON format valid
- Rate limit enforced
- Large export handled async

EDGE CASES:
- No data: return empty structure
- Export in progress: return existing job status
- CSV format: flatten nested objects

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:

- Fetch active consents from GET /api/v1/consent
- Display consent cards with service, scope, granted_at, expires_at

- Add link to export data
